facts.statement: Ceratonykus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, Maastrichtian

facts.statement: Ceratonykus was a monospecific genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur found in the Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: Ceratonykus (meaning "horned claw") is a monospecific genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from Mongolia that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in what is now the Barun Goyot Formation.

facts.statement: The genus and its only species were named and described in 2009 by Vladimir Alifanov and Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: It was named and described in 2009 by Vladimir Alifanov and Rinchen Barsbold.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton was discovered in 2003 at the Khermiin Tsav locality in Mongolia by preparator Otkhoon Zhargal.
facts.quote: In 2003, a partial skeleton of an alvarezsaurid was discovered in the Barun Goyot Formation of the Khermiin Tsav locality, Mongolia by the Paleontological Center of the Mongolian Academy of Sciences (MPC) preparator Otkhoon Zhargal.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (MPC no. 100/124) includes an incomplete skull, lower jaw, vertebrae, sternum, coracoids, a humeral fragment, forelimb elements, an ilium fragment, and hindlimbs.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MPC no. 100/124, consists of an incomplete skull and lower jaw, cervical vertebrae, caudal vertebrae, sternum, left and right coracoids, a right humeral fragment, distal elements of forelimbs, fragmentary ilium, and hindlimbs.

facts.statement: The fossil represents an adult individual, evidenced by the fusion of the astragali and tibiae and partially obliterated sutures.
facts.quote: The specimen is of an adult individual based on the fusion of the astragali and tibiae, with partially obliterated sutures.

facts.statement: Ceratonykus is estimated to have been 75 cm long and weighed 760 g.
facts.quote: Ceratonykus has an estimated length of 75 cm and weight of 760 g.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Ceratonykus to be 0.6 meters long and weigh 1 kg.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul gave Ceratonykus an estimated length of 0.6 m and weight of 1 kg.

facts.statement: Ceratonykus is characterized by a long preorbital skull region, an ovate upper temporal fenestra, frontals four times longer than wide, narrow wedge-shaped frontals, basipterygoid processes two-thirds the height of quadrates, deep mandibular fenestrae, and tightly adjoining second and fourth metatarsals.
facts.quote: Alifanov & Barsbold (2009) originally diagnosed Ceratonykus based on the long preorbital skull region; an upper temporal fenestrae ovate that was 0.4 as long as the frontals; the length of the frontal being almost four times greater than its width; the frontals narrowing towards the rostrum into a narrow wedge; the prefrontals adjoining each other towards the middle; the basipterygoid processes being two-thirds as high as the quadrates; the dentaries form a deep and rostrally tapering depression; extensive mandibular fenestrae; narrow centra of cervical and anterior caudal vertebrae; the deltopectoral crest being separated from the humeral head by a notch; the basal phalanx of the major digit of the manus is extended, with its flanks moderately wide, and a narrow and symmetrical distal condyle; the postacetabular plate of the ilia possessing a relatively small longitudinal craniomedial crest; a strongly curved femora that is nearly half as long as tibiotarsus; a distinct fourth trochanter; an undeveloped cnemial crest of the tibiae; an ascending process of the astragali that is high and wide; the tarsometatarsals being 1.33 as long as the femora; the second and fourth metatarsals tightly adjoining each other over its entire extent; a deep notch that is formed proximodorsally between the metatarsals; the second metatarsals being shorter than the fourth distally; tarsometatarsals that are 3.5 times as long as the third metatarsals; and the basal phalanx of the fourth digit of the hind feet only being slightly shorter than the basal phalanx of second digit.

facts.statement: The antorbital fenestrae were at least half the size of the orbits, while the lower temporal fenestrae were narrow and shorter than the orbit diameter.
facts.quote: The antorbital fenestrae were at least half as large as the orbits and the temporal bars are relatively small, while the lower temporal fenestrae are narrow and slightly lower in height than the diameter of the orbits.

facts.statement: The frontals were four times as long as they were wide and narrow wedge-shaped in front view, similar to Shuvuuia.
facts.quote: Both frontals are four times as long as wide, similar to Shuvuuia, and are narrow wedge-shaped in front view.

facts.statement: Ceratonykus had eyeballs positioned towards the brain with a diameter of a quarter of the head length, suggesting eyesight was a key sensory system.
facts.quote: The eyeballs would have been positioned towards the brain and are a quarter of the head length in diameter, a feature that suggests the eyesight of alvarezsaurs were the key afferent system.

facts.statement: The original describers suggested alvarezsaurs were ornithischians rather than theropods, but this hypothesis has not been accepted.
facts.quote: Its describers questioned the traditional placement of alvarezsaurs in Theropoda, instead suggesting they were ornithischians, but this has not been accepted since.

facts.statement: Ceratonykus has been considered a possible junior synonym of Parvicursor.
facts.quote: It has been considered as a possible junior synonym of Parvicursor.

facts.statement: The genus name Ceratonykus means "horned claw" derived from Greek words for horned and claw.
facts.quote: The generic name, Ceratonykus, is derived from the Greek words "ceratinus" (horned) and "onyx" (claw).

facts.statement: The species name oculatus means "sharp-sighted" or "big-eyed" derived from Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name, oculatus, is derived from the Latin word "oculatus" (sharp-sighted, big-eyed).

facts.statement: The optic lobes were displaced towards the anterior, a characteristic shared with extant birds.
facts.quote: The optic lobes are displaced towards the anterior, which is a characteristic of extant birds.

facts.statement: In Ceratonykus, the second metatarsal was shorter than the fourth metatarsal.
facts.quote: the second metatarsals were shorter than the fourth metatarsals

facts.statement: Alifanov and Barsbold (2009) originally classified Ceratonykus within the clade Parvicursoridae as the sister taxon to Mononykus.
facts.quote: Alifanov & Barsbold (2009) originally placed Ceratonykus within Alvarezsauria, within the clade Parvicursoridae, as sister taxon to Mononykus

facts.statement: Agnolin et al. (2012) placed Ceratonykus in the tribe Ceratonykini as the sister taxon to Xixianykus and Albinykus.
facts.quote: Agnolin et al. (2012) positioned Ceratonykus within the tribe Ceratonykini, as sister taxon to Xixianykus and Albinykus

facts.statement: Ceratonykus lived alongside other alvarezsaurids including Khulsanurus, Ondogurvel, and Parvicursor.
facts.quote: The fauna of the Barun Goyot Formation consists of the alvarezsaurids Khulsanurus, Ondogurvel and Parvicursor

facts.statement: Ceratonykus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Ceratonykus is known from the Barun Goyot Formation, which has been dated to the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period

facts.statement: The environment where Ceratonykus lived had a semi-arid climate with significant rainfall.
facts.quote: Overall, the formation had a semi-arid climate with significant rainfall

facts.statement: Alifanov and Savelyev proposed that the ancestors of alvarezsaurs were likely arboreal based on the cerebellum of Ceratonykus.
facts.quote: the authors proposed that the ancestor of alvarezsaurs were likely arboreal

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the complex cerebellum of Ceratonykus was useful for regulating speed and movement patterns like jumping in terrestrial alvarezsaurs.
facts.quote: the complex cerebellum could have been useful for efficient regulation of the speed and numerous movement patterns such as jumping in terrestrial alvarezsaurs

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ceratonykus is a distinct genus or a junior synonym of Parvicursor, with some researchers arguing differences are due to ontogeny or individual variation.
facts.quote: Averianov & Lopatin (2022b) considered Ceratonykus to be a junior synonym of Parvicursor as the differences between both taxa were minimal and concerned characters that are likely to be ontogenetic and possibly also individual variation

facts.statement: Ceratonykus oculatus is the only known species in the extinct genus Ceratonykus, a theropod dinosaur belonging to the Alvarezsauridae family.
facts.quote: Ceratonykus oculatus ("garra de cuernos con testigo ocular") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Ceratonykus de dinosaurio terópodo alvarezsáurido

facts.statement: Ceratonykus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 y 71 millones de años en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Ceratonykus were discovered in the Baruun Goyot Formation in Mongolia, and the type species is C. oculatus.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles fueron encontrados en la Formación Baruun Goyot, Mongolia y la especie tipo es C. oculatus

facts.statement: The genus was described based on a single holotype specimen, MPD100/120, which is a fragmentary skeleton including a skull and jaw.
facts.quote: Descrito a partir del único espécimen, el holotipo ,MPD100/120 , un esqueleto fragmentario con cráneo y mandíbula

facts.statement: Ceratonykus differs from other alvarezsaurids by having a short femur, long tarsometatarsals, and considerably reduced third metatarsials.
facts.quote: Este difiere de otros alvarezsáuridos en muchas características, incluyendo el fémur corto, los tarsometatarsales largos, y los considerablemente reducidos terceros metatarsiales

facts.statement: The endocranium of Ceratonykus features large auditory tubercles on the ventral side of the optic lobes in the mid-brain and lacks a vertical flexure in the brain floor.
facts.quote: El endocráneo muestra grandes tubérculos auditivos en ventral de los lóbulos ópticos en el cerebro medio y la ausencia de la flexura vertical en el piso del encéfalo

facts.statement: Data from the endocranium mold casts doubt on the position of Alvarezsauridae within Theropoda.
facts.quote: Los datos obtenidos del molde del endocráneo pone en duda la posición de Alvarezsauridae en Theropoda

facts.statement: Ceratonykus is classified under the parent group Parvicursorinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Parvicursorinae

facts.statement: Ceratonykus belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Alvarezsauridae

facts.statement: The time range for Ceratonykus is the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
